rationale: The Living Room Cam showed RSSI -84 dBm (below the -80 dBm threshold that causes intermittent disconnections), and the customer had moved the base station to the study behind two concrete walls. After relocating the base station back to the hallway, the camera stayed online all day, confirming weak signal as the root cause and resolving the issue at frontline.

repair_steps: Confirm the Living Room Cam has remained online since moving the base station back to the hallway.
Check the camera's RSSI in Device Settings > Device Info to ensure it is above -80 dBm.
Advise the customer to keep the base station in a central location with minimal obstructions between it and the cameras.
If the customer wants to move the base station again, recommend using the RP-1 repeater to maintain signal strength.

results.text: Peripherals talk to the base station over a sub-GHz proprietary radio. Signal strength (RSSI) is shown in Device Settings > Device Info. Above -70 dBm is good, -70 to -80 dBm is acceptable, below -80 dBm causes intermittent disconnections, delayed notifications and choppy live view. Concrete walls, metal doors and fridges strongly attenuate the signal. Fix: move the device or base station, or install the official RP-1 repeater.

complaint: My living room camera keeps going offline a few times a day, then comes back by itself. The other devices seem fine. It started about a week ago, around when we rearranged the flat and I moved the base station into the study to free up a socket in the hallway. I've restarted the camera several times and checked that it is plugged in properly. My partner thinks the camera is faulty and wants to return it, but I'd rather not buy anything new if I can avoid it.
usability_reason: Clear, polite, and actionable: it correctly ties the issue to the base station relocation and concrete walls, and recommends keeping the base station central plus a repeater option. It avoids overclaiming by framing the fix as supported by the customer's report that the camera stayed online all day. Minor deduction: it asks the customer to check RSSI even though they already said they couldn't find that reading, and it doesn't acknowledge that limitation.
